articles.title: Peacock orders 3-part Wendy Williams docuseries: Clap if You Care
articles.description: https://instagram.com/p/DccWyTxlKJc Peacock will be home to a new docuseries about Wendy Williams in 2027, titled Clap If You Care: The Wendy Williams Show . The series will follow Williams on her journey from radio host to iconic daytime talk TV host, featuring interviews from over 20 former show staffers. "But the docuseries also promises to explore the more complicated side of Williams' career, shining a light on what this meteoric rise cost the TV host. It also promises to answer long-lingering questions about Williams' exit from her own show." Sources: 1 , 2

articles.title: The TV Show That’s Better Than Ever After 23 Seasons
articles.description: Todd Williamson/Bravo It was around the time the fifth glass in the wine pairing was poured with a sidecar pre-dessert treat of coffee with rum that I turned to Top Chef judge Gail Simmons, sitting to my right, and asked sheepishly, “When you guys are taping, do you drink this much at all your dinners?” She let out a loud laugh and an emphatic, “No!” just as it was time to raise a glass again, this time to Top Chef Season 23 winner Rhoda Magbitang, who just finished serving us a tasting menu of exquisite Filipino food: lumpia, langoustine lugaw, pork belly adobo, oxtail, and a truly gluttonous amount of local specialties—including a surprise “snack” of pig ear skewers. We’re at the historic James Beard House in New York City’s Greenwich Village, the culinary cathedral where the legendary “dean of American cookery” once lived—legend is that the alcove in the southeast corner of the dining room is where Beard used to sleep with his large bare feet sticking out the window—and is now the venue for career-milestone meals prepared by the country’s greatest chefs. Read more at The Daily Beast.
